name: Mill Network at Kinderdijk-Elshout
description: Nineteen towering windmills line the canals of the Alblasserwaard polder in South Holland, near the village of Kinderdijk. Most were built in 1738 and 1740 to pump water off low-lying farmland, and together they form the largest cluster of old windmills in the Netherlands. Alongside the dykes, reservoirs and pumping stations, they show how the Dutch have kept their land dry since the Middle Ages.
